articles.title: What the Dojo is
articles.summary: A Lorcana sandbox: play both sides, rewind any turn and try another line, or study a Duels.ink game.
articles.body:
The Practice Dojo is a Lorcana sandbox. You put two decks on the table and play the game out by hand, both sides, at your own pace.

## What you can do

- **Practise a match.** Seat your deck and an opponent's, press **Start match**, and play both players' turns. See [Start your first match](help:first-match).
- **Rewind and try another line.** Every turn you end is saved to the **Multiverse**. Go back to any turn, press **Play from here**, and play it differently. The old line stays. See [What the Multiverse is](help:multiverse).
- **Study a Duels.ink game.** Paste a Duels.ink log or drop a replay file on the home screen, and every turn of that game becomes a turn you can open and replay. See [Study a Duels.ink game](help:import-overview).
- **Practise an opener.** Mulligan with real draw odds, or pick your seven by hand. See [Mulligan and your opening hand](help:mulligan).

## You are the referee

The Dojo keeps the board, counts ink, damage and lore, and saves every turn. It doesn't play for the other side and it doesn't stop you breaking a rule: you can play a card you can't afford, ink twice in a turn, or challenge with a character that's still drying. When a challenge breaks a rule, the log says so.

## Good to know

- Nothing to install and no account needed. Your sessions and decks are kept in this browser. Signing in is optional.
- Card text and art come from an online card database, so the first visit needs a connection.

articles.title: Start your first match
articles.summary: Seat two decks (or paste a list), press Start match, and settle your opening hand.
articles.body:
A match starts on the home screen: put a deck in each seat under **On the table**, then press **Start match**.

## Seat two decks

**On the table** has two seats: **You** (Player 1) and **Opponent** (Player 2).

- **Pick a built-in or saved deck:** press one of the deck chips under the seats. It goes to the first open seat. With both seats taken, it replaces the opponent.
- **Paste a decklist:** paste it into the big field at the top (one card per line, like `4 Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy`). The readout under it says how many cards it recognised. Press **Play it as you** or **Play against it**, or **Save to My decks** to keep it.
- **No list to hand?** Press **A decklist** under the field to try an example.

[Show me](show:seats)

Each seat shows the deck's name and card count. The count is marked when it isn't 60. Press **×** on a seat to empty it.

## Start the match

Press **Start match**. Both players draw seven, and Player 1's turn opens on the mulligan: keep the hand or send cards back. See [Mulligan and your opening hand](help:mulligan).

[Show me](show:start-match)

## Good to know

- **You** is Player 1 and goes first. You play both sides; see [You play both sides](help:you-play-both-sides).
- An empty seat plays 60 random cards.
- Next time, the home screen seats the same saved decks again (a pasted list isn't kept unless you save it).
- The match saves itself to this device as you play. Come back to it from **Pick up again** on the home screen.

articles.title: The screen at a glance
articles.summary: Where everything is on the board: the top bar, both halves, your hand, ink, lore, deck, discard and the side panels.
articles.body:
The board is split in two: the player whose turn it is sits at the bottom, the other player at the top. When the turn ends, the two halves swap.

## The top bar

:::desktop
- **Left:** **‹ Dojo** back to the home screen, the session's title (click to rename), then **Save**, **Save as copy** and **Share**.
- **Centre:** **Undo**, the turn chip (`TURN 16 → Player 2`) and **Challenge**.
- **Right:** **Multiverse** and **Tweaks**.
:::

:::phone
From left to right: **☰** (the side panel), **Undo**, the turn chip, **Challenge**, **Multiverse** and **⋯**. The **⋯** menu holds **Save**, **Save as copy**, **Share link**, **Tweaks** and **Leave to the dojo**.
:::

[Show me](show:topbar)

## Each player's half

:::desktop
Each half is labelled `P1 · TO PLAY` or `P2 · WAITING`. It holds:

- **The play area**, where characters, items and locations sit.
- **Discard**: a list of the cards in it, with a magnifier to look through them.
- **The ink bar**: ready ink (`4 /7 READY`), **−** / **+**, **Ready all** and the ink cards.
- **Deck**: the count. Click it to draw.
- **Lore**: the big number, with **−** and **+**.

The bottom half also has your hand and the **Turn N notes** box. The top half has the other player's hand face down, with **Hold to Reveal Hand**.
:::

:::phone
Each player has one bar: **Lore** with **−** / **+**, **Ink** with its count and pips (tap it for the inkwell), then the discard (its top card and count) and the deck (tap to draw, **⋮** for more). Under the board, the hand tray holds **Quest**, `Hand · N` and **End turn**, with your hand peeking up from the bottom edge.
:::

[Show me](show:board)

## The side panels

:::desktop
The left rail holds the players (deck and hand counts), the mini multiverse, the card preview (hover a card for details), the game log, **Auto-save every turn**, **Quest** and **End turn**. The right pane shows **Draw Odds** for the player to play.
:::

:::phone
**☰** opens the side panel: the players, the card preview, the game log, **Auto-save every turn**, **Quest** and **End turn**. Phones have no draw odds pane, mini multiverse or notes box; see [Turn notes](help:turn-notes) for writing a note.
:::

[Show me](show:sidebar)

## Good to know

- The colour of a half follows the player, not the position: Player 1 keeps their colour when they move to the top.
- On a phone or tablet, tap a card to open the card drawer with all its actions. See [Act on a card in play](help:card-actions).

articles.title: You play both sides
articles.summary: The Dojo has no opponent AI: you take both turns, and the board shows whose turn it is.
articles.body:
There's no computer opponent in the Dojo. You play Player 1's turn, end it, then play Player 2's turn, and so on. That's how you test a line against the best answer you can think of.

## Whose turn it is

The turn chip in the top bar says it: `TURN 3 → Player 2`. The player to play always sits on the **bottom** half of the board, labelled `TO PLAY`; the other player sits at the top, labelled `WAITING`.

[Show me](show:turn)

When you end the turn, the halves swap: the other player moves to the bottom and their turn begins. See [End your turn](help:end-turn).

## The other player's hand

The waiting player's hand is face down at the top of the board.

:::desktop
Hold **Hold to Reveal Hand** to see it, and let go to hide it again.
:::

:::phone
Tap **Hold to Reveal Hand** to show it, and tap again to hide it.
:::

Peeking is noted in the log. The hand hides again when the turn ends.

## Good to know

- You can still act on the waiting player's cards: damage them, banish them, change their lore or draw for them. The Dojo doesn't stop you.
- The sidebar lists **Player 1 (You)** and **Player 2**. "You" is just the seat that goes first.

articles.title: Guided tours
articles.summary: Short tours that point at the real controls on a practice board. Nothing you do in a tour is saved.
articles.body:
A guided tour points at the real controls one at a time and waits while you try each one. There are three, a few minutes each:

- **Your first turn**: the mulligan, the board, inking and playing a card, reading a card, ending the turn, playing the other side, [Undo](help:undo) and where the [Multiverse](help:multiverse) is.
- **The Multiverse**: on a copy of the Set 13 demo. Open it, read and select a node, **Play from here**, branches, saving the turn you're in, the plot view, and the mini map (desktop) or the thumb keys (phone).
- **Study a Duels.ink game**: the paste field, the example log, the readout, **Study this game** and the imported turns in the Multiverse.

## Start a tour

:::desktop
Open Help (the **?** in the top bar, or {key:?}). The tours are at the top of the list; a ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

:::phone
Open Help from the **⋯** menu, or **Help** on the home screen. The tours are at the top of the list; a ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

New players also see **Start tour** under the headline on the home screen. **Not now** hides it for good.

## During a tour

- Each step names the control to use. Steps that wait for you have **Skip this step**; the others have **Next** and **Back**.
- **Learn more** opens the article for that step. Close Help and the tour carries on.

:::desktop
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card, or {key:Esc}.
:::

:::phone
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card.
:::

## Good to know

- A tour plays on a practice board, marked **Practice · not saved**. Nothing you do there goes in your library, and the match you had open is waiting, as it was, when the tour ends.
- Want to keep the practice board? **Save a copy** in its banner makes it a session of your own, and ends the tour.
- Reloading the page ends a tour. Start it again from Help.

articles.title: Mulligan and your opening hand
articles.summary: Each player's first turn opens on their mulligan: keep the seven, or mark cards to send to the bottom and draw again.

headings.text: Read the hand before you choose

articles.body:
Each player's first turn opens on the mulligan. Player 1 chooses as the match starts. Player 2 chooses when Player 1 ends their first turn, before Player 2's draw, so they choose from the seven they were dealt.

## Keep or send cards back

The dialog shows your seven, cheapest first. The head says whether you're **on the play** (no draw turn 1) or **on the draw** (you draw one once you've chosen).

:::desktop
Click a card to mark it to go to the bottom; click it again to unmark it. To read a card, click the magnifier in its corner: the card grows in place. Any click or {key:Esc} puts it back.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card to mark it to go to the bottom; tap it again to unmark it. To read a card, {gesture:long-press} it: it shows large with its name, cost and type. Tap anywhere to close it; that tap marks nothing.
:::

A marked card sinks and shows `↓ Bottom`. Then press the one button at the foot:

- **Keep hand** when nothing is marked: the hand stays and the deck isn't touched.
- **Mulligan N cards** otherwise: the marked cards go to the bottom of the deck, you draw as many from the top, then the deck is shuffled.

[Show me](show:mulligan-confirm)

## Read the hand before you choose

Under the hand, the readout follows your marks: the **Curve** of the cards you'd keep (the ones going back show dashed), **Inkable** (how many you'd keep can be inked) and the plan (`5 kept + 2 redraw`).

**Draw odds** show your chance to find each card: **RD** among the redraws, then within the next turns' draws. Phones show the top three rows; press **All** for the rest.

[Show me](show:mulligan-readout)

## After a mulligan

The dialog stays open on your new hand. The new cards carry a **NEW** tag and the readout says how many went back and were drawn. You can't mark cards again. Press **Start turn** (or **Draw and start turn** for Player 2) to play.

## Good to know

- Nothing else works until the hand is settled: no hotkeys, and the turn can't end.
- **Craft hand** picks your seven by hand instead. See [Craft a starting hand](help:craft-hand).
- **Undo** after the turn has started brings the mulligan back.
- Leave for the home screen mid-mulligan and the dialog is waiting when you come back.

articles.title: Craft a starting hand
articles.summary: Pick your seven from the whole deck instead of drawing them, to practise a specific opener.
articles.body:
Crafting lets you choose your opening hand card by card, so you can practise one opener again and again.

## Craft your opening hand

1. When your mulligan opens, press **Craft hand** (**Craft** on a phone). [Show me](show:craft-hand)
2. **Craft Starting Hand** shows every different card in your deck, cheapest first. Each says how many you've picked of how many the deck has (`1/4`).
3. Add a copy by clicking (or tapping) the card. You can't pick more copies than the deck has, or more than seven cards.

:::mouse
Right-click a card to take one copy back out.
:::

:::touch
To start over, press **Clear**.
:::

4. When **Selected** reads `7 / 7`, press **Confirm Hand**. The rest of the deck is shuffled and your turn starts. Player 2 draws for the turn first, as usual.

## Good to know

- **Back** (or **×**) returns to the mulligan without changing anything.
- Crafting takes the place of the mulligan: once you confirm, the opening hand is settled.
- Changed your mind? **Undo** brings the mulligan back.

articles.title: Drawing cards
articles.summary: You draw at the start of your turn automatically; draw more from the deck any time.
articles.body:
Each turn's draw happens on its own: when a turn begins, the player to play draws one card. Player 1 doesn't draw on their first turn.

## Draw another card

:::desktop
Click the deck slab on that player's half. The card goes to their hand. You can also drag the top card of the deck to the hand, the play area or the ink bar.
:::

:::phone
Tap the deck on that player's bar. The card goes to their hand.
:::

[Show me](show:deck)

This works for either player's deck, so card effects that make the other player draw are one click away.

## Good to know

- Extra draws are logged and counted in the turn's **Drawn** recap.
- An empty deck just doesn't draw. The Dojo doesn't end the game for it.
- To look through the deck or shuffle it, use the deck's other controls. See [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
- Made a mistake? **Undo** puts the card back.

articles.title: Ink a card
articles.summary: Put a card from your hand into your inkwell, face down, to pay for cards later.

headings.text: See what you inked this turn

articles.body:
Ink a card to grow your inkwell. Ink pays for the cards you play. A card goes in ready, so you can spend it the turn you ink it.

## Ink a card

:::desktop
Drag a card from your hand onto your ink bar; anywhere on the bar takes it. Or hover the card and press **INK**, or click it and choose **Add to Inkwell**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, press **Ink**. Or drag the card up onto the ink count on your player bar.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-bar)

## See what you inked this turn

A card inked this turn shows face up in the inkwell, and the count gets a tag: **+1** on desktop, **+1 inked** on a phone. Until you ink, a phone's bar says **No ink yet**. The cards turn face down when that player's next turn begins.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't enforce one ink a turn: the tag just shows how many you've inked.
- **INK**, **Add to Inkwell** and **Ink** only appear for a card with the inkwell symbol (a phone shows **No ink** instead). Dragging doesn't check, so you can ink any card.
- To take it back, press **Undo**, or move the ink card to your hand. See [Your inkwell](help:inkwell).

articles.title: Your inkwell: ready, spend, ready all
articles.summary: Read your ready ink, spend or ready it by hand, and act on a single ink card.
articles.body:
Your inkwell shows how much ink you have ready out of how much you have. Playing a card spends ink for you; these controls are for everything else, like an ability that costs ink.

## Read your ink

:::desktop
The ink bar reads `4 /7 READY`: four ready of seven. Spent ink cards are dimmed and turned. The ink cards sit on the right of the bar, overlapping once they don't fit.
:::

:::phone
Your player bar shows `4/7` and a pip for each ink, dimmed when spent.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-bar)

## Spend or ready ink

:::desktop
On the ink bar, **−** spends one ink, **+** readies one, and **Ready all** readies the lot.
:::

:::phone
Tap the ink count to open the inkwell. **−** spends one, **+** readies one, **Ready all** readies the lot. **×** or a tap outside closes it.
:::

## Act on one ink card

:::desktop
Click an ink card. It opens in place with **Exert** (or **Ready**), **To hand** and **Discard**. Click it again, click elsewhere or press {key:Esc} to put it down.
:::

:::phone
In the inkwell, tap an ink card, then **Exert** (or **Ready**), **To hand** or **Discard** in the bar underneath.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-panel)

## Good to know

- Both players' inkwells work the same way, so you can fix the waiting player's ink too.
- Ink readies by itself at the start of that player's turn.
- If you play a card you can't afford, no ink is spent. Spend it by hand with **−** if you need to.

articles.title: Play a card
articles.summary: Move a card from your hand onto the field; the Dojo spends the ink for you.
articles.body:
Play a card from your hand to put it into play. If you have enough ready ink, the Dojo spends the card's cost for you.

## Play a card

:::desktop
Drag the card from your hand onto your play area; anywhere in the area takes it. Or hover the card and press **PLAY**, or click it and choose **Play Card (-3 Ink)**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand to open the card drawer. It shows the cost and your ready ink. Press **Play · −3 ink**. Or drag the card up onto the board.
:::

[Show me](show:hand)

A character comes in **drying**: it shows a **NEW** tag and can't quest until your next turn. Songs and actions land in play too; when they're done, banish them to send them to the discard.

## Not enough ink?

You can still play it. The Dojo plays the card and spends no ink, so you can test a line you can't quite afford. On a phone the key says so: **Play anyway · 2 short**.

## Good to know

- To shift a card or play a character straight to a location, drag it onto that card instead. See [Locations, shift and cards under](help:locations-and-stacks).
- Card abilities don't trigger by themselves. Do what the card says by hand: draw, add damage, change lore.
- **Undo** takes the play back, ink included.

articles.title: Act on a card in play (exert, ready, damage, banish)
articles.summary: Exert and ready, add or remove damage, banish, and the hover hotkeys for each.
articles.body:
Every card in play, on either side of the board, can be exerted or readied, take or lose damage, and be banished. Pick whichever way suits your device.

## Hover controls

:::desktop
Point at a card in play. A damage stepper appears on top (**−** `0/3` **+**) and a column of icon buttons down its right edge (hover one for its name): **Challenge** and **Quest** (your characters, when they can), **Exert** or **Ready**, and **Banish**.

Under every card with willpower sits a track with one segment per point. Click a segment to set the damage exactly; click the lit end segment to take one off.
:::

## Hover hotkeys

:::desktop
With the pointer over a card in play:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| {key:+} / {key:-} | add / remove one damage |
| {key:0} – {key:9} | set the damage to that number |
| {key:E} | exert or ready |
| {key:B} | banish |
| {key:C} | challenge mode, with this character picked |
:::

## The card menu

:::desktop
Right-click (or click) a card in play for its menu. **Card**: **Exert** / **Ready**, **Quest (+2 Lore)**, **Challenge…**, **Leave Location**, and a **Damage** stepper that stays open while you click it. **Move**: **Banish (To Discard)**, **Return to Hand**, **Put on Top of Deck**, **Put on Bottom of Deck**. **Stack**: **Put Top Card of Deck Under**, **Separate Stacked Cards**. Only what applies to that card shows.
:::

## The card drawer

:::touch
Tap a card in play to open the card drawer. The head says whose it is and its state (`P2 · exerted · 2 / 5`). Under the card's text:

- **Damage**: tap a segment to set it, or **− 1** / **+ 1**.
- **Challenge**, **Quest**, **Exert** (or **Ready**) and **Banish**. A key you can't use is hollow.
- **Move to**: **To hand**, **Deck top**, **Deck bottom**, **Put under**, and **Leave location** or **Separate stack** when they apply.

Step to the next card in play with **‹ ›** or a sideways {gesture:swipe} on the text. **×**, a tap outside or {key:Esc} closes it.
:::

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- Once damage reaches willpower, the card pulses and shows a **LETHAL · BANISH** button under it (the drawer says `lethal`). The Dojo doesn't banish it until you do, except after a challenge.
- A banished card goes to its owner's discard with any cards under it, its damage cleared.
- The Dojo doesn't check card effects. Exert, ready or damage anything the cards say to.
- Every change can be undone with **Undo**.

articles.title: Quest and lore
articles.summary: Quest with one character or all of them, and change lore by hand.
articles.body:
Questing exerts a character and adds its lore to its player's score. The first to 20 lore wins.

## Quest with one character

:::desktop
Hover the character and press the quest button (the diamond), or click it and choose **Quest (+2 Lore)**.
:::

:::touch
Tap the character, then **Quest** in the card drawer.
:::

You can quest with a character of the player to play that's ready, not drying, and has lore.

## Quest with everyone

Press **Quest**: every ready, dry character with lore quests at once. The number beside it says how many will. {key:Q} does the same on a keyboard.

:::desktop
**Quest** sits at the foot of the left rail, above **End turn**.
:::

:::phone
**Quest** sits in the hand tray, left of your hand.
:::

[Show me](show:quest-all)

## Change lore by hand

Press **−** or **+** beside a player's **Lore** to take one off or add one. Use it for lore from abilities and locations, or to fix a mistake. Lore never goes below 0.

[Show me](show:lore)

## Good to know

- Quest uses the lore printed on the card. Bonuses from abilities aren't added; add them with **+**.
- The Dojo doesn't check quest restrictions on cards; it's up to you.
- Hand changes to lore are noted in the log, and **Undo** takes any of it back.
- At 20 lore the Dojo tells you who won. See [Winning a game](help:winning).

articles.title: Challenge
articles.summary: Challenge an opposing card by dragging or tapping, with a forecast of what happens before you commit.
articles.body:
In a challenge, your character and the opposing card deal their strength to each other as damage. The Dojo works out the damage, exerts your character and banishes anything that ends up with damage equal to its willpower.

## Challenge mode

Press **Challenge** in the top bar (or {key:C}). A bar across the board reads **CHALLENGE MODE**. Then:

:::desktop
Drag one of your characters onto an opposing card. Or click your character, then click the target. With a character picked, hovering a target shows the forecast.
:::

:::touch
Tap one of your characters, then tap an opposing card. Once you've picked, every opposing card shows a badge with the outcome. Dragging works too.
:::

You stay in the mode to challenge again. Press **Done · Esc** to leave. {key:Esc} first drops the picked character, then leaves. Ending the turn leaves it too.

[Show me](show:challenge-mode)

## Start from a character

:::desktop
Hover your character and press its challenge button, or right-click it and choose **Challenge…**. Challenge mode opens with it picked. You can also drag your character onto an opposing card without entering the mode.
:::

:::touch
Tap your character and press **Challenge** in the card drawer. Challenge mode opens with it picked; tap the target.
:::

## The forecast

Before you commit, the Dojo shows what would happen: each card's damage after the challenge and whether it's banished (**✕ Banishes …**, **⇄ Trade**). Choose how much it shows with **Off**, **Light** or **Full** in the challenge bar. See [Challenge forecast](help:forecast).

## Good to know

- Damage is strength, plus **Challenger +N** on the challenger, minus **Resist +N** on the card taking it. Other abilities aren't applied: fix damage by hand afterwards.
- The Dojo doesn't stop an exerted or drying challenger, or a ready target. It allows them and notes it in the log.
- Bodyguard, Evasive and the like aren't checked: you're the referee.
- One **Undo** takes back the whole challenge.

articles.title: Locations, shift and cards under
articles.summary: Move characters to a location, shift onto a character, put cards under, and separate a stack.

headings.text: Move a character to a location

articles.body:
Locations sit in your play area with the characters at them above them. Shift and "put under" build a stack: one card on top, the rest underneath.

## Move a character to a location

Drag the character onto the location. A character dragged from your hand is played straight to the location, and its cost is spent.

To leave, choose **Leave Location** in the card's menu (desktop) or **Leave location** in the card drawer (touch). Or drag the character back onto an empty part of your play area.

:::touch
Dragging works on touch screens too: press the card, then move it.
:::

## Shift onto a character

Drag the new card from your hand onto the character it shifts onto. It goes on top, keeps the card underneath's damage, exerted state and location, and the log says you shifted. The badge in the corner counts the cards under it.

You can drop any of your cards onto another of yours this way; only a matching name counts as a shift.

## Put a card under

:::desktop
Right-click your card and choose **Put Top Card of Deck Under**. The deck's top card goes under it face down.
:::

:::touch
Tap your card and press **Put under** in the card drawer.
:::

## Separate a stack

Choose **Separate Stacked Cards** in the menu, or **Separate stack** in the drawer. The cards underneath come out into play, exerted and drying.

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- Dragging from your hand spends the card's full cost, not its Shift cost. Give back the difference with **+** on your ink bar.
- Moving to a location costs nothing in the Dojo: spend the move cost with **−** on your ink bar.
- A location's lore isn't added at the start of your turn. Add it with the lore **+**.
- When a card with cards under it leaves play, the cards under it go with it.
- Banish a location and the characters at it stay in play.

articles.title: Move cards: to hand, deck top or bottom, discard
articles.summary: Send any card back to the hand, the top or bottom of the deck, or the discard.
articles.body:
Card effects move cards between zones all the time. Any card in play or in a hand can go back to the hand, onto the top or bottom of the deck, or into the discard.

## From play

:::desktop
Right-click the card. Under **Move**: **Banish (To Discard)**, **Return to Hand**, **Put on Top of Deck**, **Put on Bottom of Deck**.
:::

:::touch
Tap the card. In the card drawer, **Banish**, or under **Move to**: **To hand**, **Deck top**, **Deck bottom**.
:::

## From a hand

:::desktop
Right-click the card in your hand: **Discard Card**, **Put on Top of Deck** or **Put on Bottom of Deck**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, **Discard**, or under **More**: **Deck top** or **Deck bottom**.
:::

## By dragging

:::desktop
Drag a card onto a deck (it goes on top), a discard pile or a hand. This works from play, a hand or the inkwell.
:::

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- A card leaving play loses its damage and exert, and takes any cards under it along.
- The menu and the drawer send a card to its own player's deck, hand or discard. A drag puts it where you drop it.
- Ink cards go to hand or discard from the inkwell. See [Your inkwell](help:inkwell).
- To bring a card back from the discard, see [Your discard pile](help:inspect-discard).
- **Undo** takes any move back.

articles.title: End your turn
articles.summary: End the turn: the other player readies, draws, and the turn is saved to the Multiverse if auto-save is on.
articles.body:
When you're done, end the turn. The other player's turn begins, and the board swaps so they're at the bottom.

## End the turn

:::desktop
Press **End turn →** at the foot of the left rail, or press {key:Space}.
:::

:::phone
Press **End turn** in the hand tray, right of your hand. It's also in the **☰** panel.
:::

[Show me](show:end-turn)

## What happens next

1. The other player becomes the player to play. The turn number goes up when Player 1's turn comes round.
2. **Ready step:** their characters and items ready, drying ends, and their ink readies. Cards they inked last turn turn face down. Locations aren't readied.
3. **Draw step:** they draw a card.
4. **Auto-save:** the Multiverse gets a node for the new turn, named like `Turn 4 - Player 1 Active`. It keeps your turn note and a recap of what you did (drew, inked, played, quested, banished). See [Every turn is saved](help:auto-save).

Challenge mode ends, and the other player's hand is hidden again.

## Auto-save every turn

The switch **Auto-save every turn** sits in the left rail (in the **☰** panel on a phone). It's on by default. Turn it off and ending the turn saves no node.

[Show me](show:auto-save)

## Good to know

- Player 2's first turn opens on their mulligan; their draw comes after it. See [Mulligan](help:mulligan).
- The turn can't end while a mulligan is open.
- Abilities that trigger at the start or end of a turn aren't applied: do them by hand.
- Ended too soon? **Undo** takes you back. The node it saved stays in the Multiverse.

articles.title: Undo
articles.summary: Take back the last action, as many steps as you like.
articles.body:
**Undo** takes back your last action. Press it again to keep going back, one action at a time.

## Undo an action

:::desktop
Press **Undo** in the top bar, beside the turn chip. The rail's round-arrow button at the foot does the same.
:::

:::phone
Press the round-arrow button in the top bar, left of the turn chip.
:::

[Show me](show:undo)

## What it covers

Everything you do on the board: playing, inking, moving and drawing cards, damage, exert and ready, quests and challenges, lore, ink, turn notes, the mulligan and ending the turn. The log steps back with it.

It goes back up to 250 actions, and the history is kept with the session, so it still works after you leave and come back.

## Good to know

- There's no redo. To try both versions of a turn, save the turn first and branch in the Multiverse. See [Branching](help:branches).
- Undo doesn't touch the Multiverse: a node saved when you ended a turn stays. Ending the turn again saves a new node beside it.
- **Play from here** in the Multiverse, or a jump on the mini multiverse, starts a fresh undo history.
- **Undo** has no keyboard shortcut.

articles.title: Turn notes
articles.summary: Write a note for the turn you're in; it travels with the turn into the Multiverse.
articles.body:
Write down what you're trying, or why, as you play. Each player has one note per turn, and it's saved with that turn's node in the Multiverse.

## Write a note

:::desktop
Type in the **Turn N notes** box at the bottom left of the board. It saves when you click away.
:::

:::phone
{gesture:long-press} (long press) an empty part of the board. A **Turn N notes** dialog opens with the note for the player to play. Press **Save**, or **Cancel** to leave it as it was. {key:Enter} adds a line; {key:Ctrl+Enter} saves.
:::

[Show me](show:turn-notes)

The note shows in the game log under the turn it belongs to, as **Turn N note · Player N**.

## Where the note goes

When the turn ends with auto-save on, the note goes into the new node, above the recap of the turn. **Save current unfinished turn** in the Multiverse starts its note from it too. To change a note later, edit it in the Multiverse panel. See [The Multiverse panel](help:multiverse-panel).

## Good to know

- The note belongs to the player to play and the turn number. The other player's turn starts with an empty box.
- Hotkeys don't fire while you type in the notes box.
- Saving an empty note clears it.

articles.title: Winning a game (20 lore)
articles.summary: At 20 lore the branch is won: the Dojo says so and offers the Multiverse to try other lines.
articles.body:
The first player to reach 20 lore wins. The Dojo notices, whether the lore came from a quest, **Quest** or the lore **+**.

## When a player reaches 20

A dialog says who won, the lore score and the turn. A **Game Over - Player 1 Wins!** node is saved to the Multiverse, whether auto-save is on or not. Then choose:

- **View Multiverse** to see the game as a tree and pick another turn to replay.
- **Stay Here** to keep playing on this board.

[Show me](show:lore)

## Try another line

A win is the end of one branch, not of the session. Open the **Multiverse**, select an earlier turn and press **Play from here** to play it differently. See [What the Multiverse is](help:multiverse).

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't stop the game at 20: the board stays live.
- It says so once per branch. If you **Undo** below 20 and reach it again, you get the dialog and a new node again.
- Lore isn't capped at 20, and other ways to win or lose (like an empty deck) aren't checked.

articles.title: Read a card: preview and text mode
articles.summary: See a card big with its full text: the preview on desktop, the card drawer on a phone, and text mode for every card.
articles.body:
Cards on the board are small. The preview shows one big enough to read, with all its abilities.

## See a card big

:::desktop
Point at any card: on the board, in a hand, in the discard column, in the draw odds or in a deck or discard grid. It shows in the preview in the side rail, under the mini multiverse. The last card you pointed at stays there until you point at another.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card in play or in your hand. The card drawer opens with the card's full text and a small picture of it. Step to the next card with ‹ ›, or swipe sideways on the text.

For other cards (the discard, the other player's hand), tap the card and choose **Preview Card**. The ☰ side panel opens with the card in it.
:::

[Show me](show:card-preview)

## Text mode

Turn on **Text** under **Card display** in Tweaks to show every card as text instead of art: the board, the hands, the grids and the preview. The text card has the cost (a gold disc if it can be inked, a dark hexagon if not), name, type line, every ability and the stats. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).

## Good to know

- Locations always show as text in the preview, so they aren't cropped.
- If a card's art can't load (offline, for example), the preview falls back to its text by itself.
- On a tablet, tapping a card in play opens the card drawer; a hand card's menu has **Preview Card**.

articles.title: Look through your deck and reorder it
articles.summary: Open a deck, drag its cards into the order you want, save the order, or shuffle it.
articles.body:
Open a deck to see every card left in it, in draw order, and set up the draws you want to practise.

## Open the deck

:::desktop
Click the magnifier at the top right of the deck. Or right-click the deck and choose **Inspect Deck**. Clicking the deck itself draws a card.
:::

:::phone
Tap the ⋮ button on the deck in the player bar, then **Inspect Deck**. Tapping the deck itself draws a card.
:::

[Show me](show:deck)

The grid starts with the top card: the first card is the next one drawn. This works on both players' decks.

## Reorder it

1. Drag a card onto the place you want it. The card you dropped on moves along.
2. Press **Save Custom Order**. **Cancel** (or {key:Esc}) leaves the deck as it was.

Saving also adds a node called *Custom deck ordering* to the Multiverse, so you can come back to this order.

## Shuffle it

:::desktop
Click the shuffle button at the bottom right of the deck, or right-click the deck and choose **Shuffle Deck**.
:::

:::phone
Tap ⋮ on the deck, then **Shuffle Deck**.
:::

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't stop you from stacking a deck. You're the referee.
- To change which cards are in the deck, see [Swap a card](help:swap-cards).
- **Undo** takes back a shuffle or a saved order.

articles.title: Your discard pile
articles.summary: Read the discard on the board, open it in full, and bring cards back.
articles.body:
Every card that leaves play or is discarded goes to its owner's discard pile. You can read it at any time and take cards back out.

## Read the discard

:::desktop
Each half of the board has a **Discard** column: the cards listed newest first, with cost / strength / lore on the right. Past eight cards, **+N more** shows the rest. Point at a row to see the card in the preview.
:::

:::phone
The discard is the mini card on the player bar: it shows the top card and how many cards are in the pile.
:::

[Show me](show:discard)

## Open it in full

:::desktop
Click the magnifier in the **Discard** header, or right-click the column and choose **Inspect Discard Pile**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the magnifier on the discard's mini card.
:::

The pile opens as a grid of cards, oldest first.

## Bring a card back

:::desktop
Click or right-click a card in the column or the grid. Choose **Play Card to Field**, **Return to Hand**, **Move to Top of Deck** or **Move to Bottom of Deck**. You can also drag a row from the column onto the field, the hand or the deck.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card in the grid, or the top card on the bar, and pick one of the same moves. **Preview Card** shows it big.
:::

The grid stays open, so you can take out several cards.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't check that a card is allowed to come back. You're the referee.
- **Play Card to Field** spends ink when the player has enough ready.

articles.title: Swap a card in your hand or deck
articles.summary: Replace one card, or every copy of it, with any other card to test a different list.

headings.text: Swap a card in your hand

articles.body:
Swap a card for any other card to see how a different list plays, without building a new deck.

## Swap a card in your hand

:::desktop
Right-click the card in your hand and choose **Swap Card**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, under **More**, press **Swap**.
:::

Type at least two letters of a card's name in **Search Replacement Card**, then click the card you want. It takes the old card's place in the hand straight away.

## Replace cards in the deck

1. Open the deck: see [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
2. Right-click a card in the grid and choose **Replace this card**, or **Replace all copies** to change every copy of it in the deck.
3. Search and click the new card.
4. Press **Save Custom Order**. Until you do, nothing changes: **Cancel** throws the replacements away.

:::phone
On a phone, the menu for a card in the deck grid opens with a press and hold. Some phone browsers (Safari on iPhone) don't open it.
:::

## Good to know

- The search offers every card, not just your deck's inks. The Dojo doesn't check that the new card is legal in your deck, or how many copies you have.
- **Replace all copies** only changes the cards in the deck, not the copies in your hand, in play or in the discard.
- **Undo** takes back a hand swap.
- Swaps change this match only. To change a saved deck, edit it in the Library: see [Your decks](help:decks).

articles.title: Unknown cards and filling them in
articles.summary: Imports leave cards they couldn't see as unknown; replace them one at a time or all at once.
articles.body:
When you import a Duels.ink game, any card the log or replay never shows becomes an **unknown card**: a card back with no name. You can play on with them or replace them with real cards.

## Where they show up

- **Decks.** The cards nobody drew or revealed yet. In the deck grid they show as a card back marked *(Unknown)*.
- **The opponent's hand**, when the game never revealed those cards.
- **Cards under a character** after a boost or shift in a text log.
- **Draw odds** groups them in one **Unknown** row, so you can see how many are left.

## Replace them

1. Open the deck: see [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
2. Right-click an unknown card. **Replace this card** changes that one; **Replace all copies** turns every unknown card in the deck into the card you pick.
3. Press **Save Custom Order**.

An unknown card in the other player's hand can be swapped: right-click it and choose **Swap Card**. On a phone, tap an unknown card in your hand and press **Swap** (see [Swap a card](help:swap-cards)).

## Good to know

- There's no button to fill the unknown cards from a decklist. Replace them by hand, or draw and play with them as they are.
- An unknown card has no cost or stats, so it stays out of the curve and the odds of named cards.
- Saving the order adds a node to the Multiverse, so the filled-in deck is kept with that turn.

articles.title: Draw odds
articles.summary: The chance to draw each card in your next draws, updated as the game changes.
articles.body:
**Draw odds**, on the right of the board, shows the chance of drawing at least one copy of each card in your next few draws. It follows the active player's deck and updates after every change.

[Show me](show:draw-odds)

## Read the odds

Each row is a card in the player's whole list, wherever its copies are now:

- **Left**: copies still in the deck.
- The three number columns: the chance, in percent, of drawing at least one copy within the next 1, 2 or 3 draws.

Rows with the most copies left come first. A card with no copies left stays in the list, greyed out with dashes. The number next to the title is the deck size. Point at a row to see the card in the preview.

## Change the draw windows

Click a column's number (1, 2 or 3) and type how many draws it should cover, from 1 to 60. The mulligan's odds use the same three windows.

## Hide the pane

Click the arrows at the top right of **Draw odds** to fold it into a thin strip; click them again to open it.

## Good to know

- The odds assume the deck is in random order. After you stack a deck by hand, they don't know the order you set.
- Unknown cards from an import are grouped in one **Unknown** row.
- On a phone there's no draw odds pane; the mulligan shows its own odds. See [Mulligan](help:mulligan).

articles.title: Your decks: new, import, edit
articles.summary: Paste or import a decklist, save it to My decks, edit it, and seat it for a match.

headings.text: Add a deck in the Library

articles.body:
Keep the decks you play in **My decks**, so they're one tap away on the home screen.

## Paste a decklist

Paste a list into the field on the home screen, one card per line, like `4 Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy`. The readout under it says what it understood: the inks, and how many of the 60 cards it recognised (and which lines it skipped). Then choose:

- **Play it as you** or **Play against it** to seat it for the next match.
- **Save to My decks** to keep it.

[Show me](show:intake)

## Add a deck in the Library

Open **Library**, then **Decks**:

- **New deck**: type a name, paste the list, add notes if you like, and press **Save deck**.
- **Import .txt**: pick a text file with a decklist. It opens in the same form to check and save.
- **From a replay**: pick a Duels.ink replay file (.json, .replay or .replay.gz). The form fills with your exact 60 from that game.

[Show me](show:deck-new)

## Edit, seat or delete

Each deck has **You** and **Opponent** to seat it. Its **⋯** menu has **Edit**, **Share a link** and **Delete…**. Saving an edit updates a seat that holds that deck.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't check deck rules. A list that isn't 60 cards plays with the cards it has, and the seat's count turns amber.
- If no card is recognised, the deck is 60 random cards.
- My decks live in this browser. Signing in keeps them in your account too: see [The Library](help:library).

articles.title: Built-in decks and demos
articles.summary: Ready-made decks for each set and example sessions to explore, all without signing in.
articles.body:
The Dojo comes with a few decks and example games, so you can start without a list of your own.

## Play a built-in deck

On the home screen, under **On the table**, pick a deck chip. It goes to the first open seat (**You**, then **Opponent**). Press **Start match**.

[Show me](show:deck-chips)

The Library's **Decks** tab lists them on the **Built in** shelf, grouped by set, with **You** and **Opponent** to seat them. To make your own version, open its **⋯** menu and choose **Copy to my decks and edit**.

## Explore a demo

Under **Pick up again**, the demos are marked *Demo · opens as your own copy*. Press **Explore** to open one: a full game with its Multiverse, to step through and play from any turn.

[Show me](show:recent)

## Good to know

- A demo opens as a copy in your sessions. Change it as much as you like; the demo itself stays the same.
- Built-in decks are the same for everyone and can't be edited in place.
- **A decklist**, under the paste field, puts a built-in list in the field to try.
- An empty seat plays 60 random cards.

articles.title: What the Multiverse is
articles.summary: Every saved turn is a node in a tree; jump to any of them and play a different line from there.
articles.body:
The Multiverse keeps every turn you've saved, so you can go back to any of them and play it another way.

Each saved board is a **node**. Nodes link up turn by turn into a line: the game as you played it. Go back to an earlier node, play on from it, and the new turns grow a second line from that point: a branch. All the lines together make a tree, and that tree is the Multiverse. It's how you answer "what if I had challenged instead of quested on turn 6?": play both and compare.

## Open the Multiverse

:::desktop
Click **Multiverse** in the top bar, or press {key:M}. Press {key:M} or {key:Esc} again, or the ✕, to go back to the board.
:::

:::phone
Tap the branch icon in the top bar. Tap ✕ to go back to the board.
:::

[Show me](show:multiverse)

## What you see

- **The canvas** draws the tree, the earliest turns on the left. The path from the start to the node you're on is highlighted; the other lines are grey.
- **The panel** sits beside the canvas (under it on a phone). It shows the node you select, with **Play from here**, and holds **Save current unfinished turn**.

[Show me](show:tree-panel)

## Good to know

- Nodes come from [auto-save](help:auto-save) at the end of each turn, from [saving the turn you're in](help:save-unfinished-turn), and from imported Duels.ink games. When a player reaches 20 lore, the Dojo also saves a **Game Over** node that closes the branch.
- Selecting a node only shows it. Your board changes when you press **Play from here**.
- Jumping never loses the board you leave: see ["Left here" snapshots](help:left-here).
- The tree is part of the session: it's saved with it, and **Export** in the Multiverse header writes the session to a file, tree included.

articles.title: Every turn is saved
articles.summary: With auto-save on, ending a turn saves the board as a node in the Multiverse.
articles.body:
With **Auto-save every turn** on, each **End turn** adds a node to the Multiverse, so the whole game is saved turn by turn without you doing anything.

## Turn auto-save on or off

:::desktop
The **Auto-save every turn** switch sits at the foot of the side rail, above **Quest** and **End turn**.

[Show me](show:auto-save)
:::

:::phone
Open the ☰ menu. The **Auto-save every turn** switch is near the bottom, above **Quest** and **End turn**.

[Show me](show:menu)
:::

## What an auto-save keeps

When you end a turn, the next player readies and draws, and then the Dojo saves the board as a node. Its name says the turn and the player about to play: **Turn 5 - Player 2 Active** holds the board at the start of Player 2's turn 5. The node also keeps:

- the note written for the turn that just ended (see [Turn notes](help:turn-notes)),
- a **Turn recap** of that turn: what was drawn, inked, played, shifted, discarded, quested and banished,
- the cards behind the recap, in sections such as **Played**, **Inked** and **Drawn**.

The new node hangs off the node you were on, so the tree follows the line you're playing.

## Good to know

- With the switch off, ending a turn saves nothing. Save by hand with [Save current unfinished turn](help:save-unfinished-turn).
- The switch is on each time you open the Dojo; turning it off lasts until you reload.
- On turn 1, the node waits until Player 2 has settled their mulligan and drawn, so it holds the board Player 2 plays from.
- When a player reaches 20 lore, the Dojo saves a **Game Over** node even with auto-save off.

articles.title: Save the turn you're in
articles.summary: Save the board mid-turn as a node, with a name and a note.
articles.body:
Save the board as it is right now, in the middle of a turn, as a node you can come back to: before a risky challenge, say, or at a moment you want to study later.

## Save current unfinished turn

:::desktop
Press {key:T} on the board, or open the Multiverse and click **Save current unfinished turn** at the top of the panel.
:::

:::phone
Open the Multiverse and tap **Save current unfinished turn** at the top of the panel, under the canvas.
:::

[Show me](show:save-turn)

The button opens a short form:

1. **Name** starts as **Turn 7 - Player 1 (unfinished)**. Change it to say what the node is for.
2. **Note** starts with your turn note and a recap of what you've done so far this turn (drew, inked, played…). Edit it freely; Markdown works.
3. **This node keeps** shows the cards the node will record, by section.
4. Press **Save node**. **Cancel** closes the form without saving.

:::desktop
In the **Name** field, {key:Enter} saves. {key:Esc} closes the form.
:::

## Good to know

- Your board doesn't change: carry on playing. The new node hangs off the node you were on and becomes the one you're on, so the next auto-save hangs off it.
- You can rename the node or change its note later in [the panel](help:multiverse-panel).
- **Save as copy** in the top bar is something else: it copies the whole session.

articles.title: Reading a node
articles.summary: What a node shows: whose turn, the lore, the note, the turn recap and the cards played.
articles.body:
A node is one saved board. In the cards view each node is a small card; this is how to read it. (A phone opens the Multiverse on the plot; tap **Plot**, the grid of dots in the header, for the cards. See [Cards and plot](help:multiverse-views).)

## What's on a node

- **Tone:** a light card is Player 1's turn, a dark card Player 2's. The deck icon says the same.
- **Name:** an auto-save is called **Turn 16 - Player 2 Active**: the board at the start of that player's turn. A turn you saved yourself ends in **(unfinished)**.
- **Subline:** the turn, the lore (**P1: 10 - P2: 11**) and the time it was saved.
- **Note:** a dark box with the turn's note and its **Turn recap** (drew, inked, played…). Click it to edit it in the panel.
- **Played:** the cards played that turn.
- **The bin** deletes the node (with **Undo**).

## Which node is which

- **The node you're on** (your board came from it) has a coloured border and foot, and the path to it is highlighted. The panel calls it **· you are here**.
- **The selected node** (the one the panel shows) has four corner marks around it.
- **A "Left here" snapshot** has a dashed outline and a dashed line to its node. See ["Left here" snapshots](help:left-here).
- **A won branch** ends in a **Game Over** node with a trophy, a plate with the winner's lore and **Branch closed**, and a short bar after it.

## Every card section

Select a node to see all its card sections in the panel: **Played**, **Inked**, **Drawn**, **Discarded**, **Banished**, **Quested** and **Starting hand**. In **Starting hand**, cards that left the hand that turn are crossed out. To show every section inside every node, turn on **Show in nodes** under **Turn recap** in the panel.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Good to know

- The name and the note are yours to change: see [The panel](help:multiverse-panel).
- On an auto-save, **Turn recap** lists the turn that just ended, not the one the board is about to play.

articles.title: The panel: select, play from here, rename, notes, delete
articles.summary: Select a node to read it in the panel, play from it, rename it, edit its note or delete it.
articles.body:
The panel shows the node you select. Read it there first, then play from it, rename it, change its note or delete it.

## Select a node

:::desktop
Click a node, or a dot in the plot. The arrow keys move the selection (see [Moving around](help:multiverse-navigate)).
:::

:::phone
Tap a node or a dot, or move the cursor with the thumb keys. The panel is under the canvas: scroll down to read all of it.
:::

Selecting doesn't touch your board. The panel shows **Selected** (with **· you are here** on the node you're on), the name, the turn, lore and time, the note, **Lore race to 20** and the **Turn recap** as cards.

[Show me](show:selected-node)

## Play from here

Press **Play from here**. The board becomes that node's board and the Multiverse closes.

:::desktop
Or double-click the node, or press {key:Enter}.
:::

If the board you left wasn't saved, it's kept as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here).

## Rename a node

Click its name in the panel, type, and press {key:Enter} (or click away). {key:Esc} cancels.

## Edit the note

Click the note, or **Add a note…** when it's empty. The whole text is yours to edit, turn recap included; Markdown works. Click away to save. {key:Esc} cancels.

:::desktop
{key:Ctrl+Enter} saves too. Clicking a note on a node opens it here.
:::

## Delete a node

Press the bin, in the panel or on the node. Its later turns aren't lost: they move up to hang off the node before it. The toast offers **Undo**.

## Good to know

:::desktop
The panel docks on the right. The columns button in the Multiverse header moves it to the left (or back), and the Dojo remembers the side. [Show me](show:tree-dock)
:::

- A "Left here" snapshot has **Keep as node** instead of a name and note to edit.

articles.title: Branching: try another line
articles.summary: Play from an earlier node and do something different: the new turns grow a new branch.
articles.body:
To try another line, go back to an earlier node and play on from it. The new turns grow a new branch, and the line you played before stays exactly as it was.

## Try another line

1. Open the Multiverse and select the node to go back to. An auto-save named **Turn 6 - Player 1 Active** is the board at the start of Player 1's turn 6, so pick it to replay that turn.
2. Press **Play from here**. You're back on the board, at that point in the game.
3. Play the turn differently and end it. With auto-save on, the new node hangs off the one you played from, beside the turn that followed before: that's a branch.
4. Keep playing. Every turn you end adds to the new line.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Compare the lines

The path to the node you're on is highlighted; the other lines are grey. Select nodes on each line and compare their **Lore race to 20** and **Turn recap** in the panel. The plot shows the whole game at once (see [Cards and plot](help:multiverse-views)).


## Good to know

- Branching never changes or deletes the nodes you already have.
- The board you leave is kept as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here) if it wasn't saved.
- **Undo** doesn't reach across a jump: its history starts fresh from the node you play from.
- When a player reaches 20 lore, a **Game Over** node closes the branch, and the Dojo offers **View Multiverse** or **Stay Here**. You can still go back and play a branch where the other player wins.

articles.title: "Left here" snapshots
articles.summary: When you jump away from an unsaved board, the Dojo keeps it as a dashed "Left here" snapshot.
articles.body:
When you jump to another node from a board you haven't saved, the Dojo keeps that board as a "Left here" snapshot first. A jump never loses your work.

## When a snapshot is kept

Every jump checks the board you're leaving: **Play from here**, and on desktop a double-click, {key:Enter} or a click in the mini multiverse. If the board has changed since it was loaded or saved, it's kept as a snapshot. If it's exactly a node or snapshot that's still in the tree, nothing is added.

## Find a snapshot

%%%TODO: Add a screenshot of a snapshot

A snapshot hangs off the node you were last on, on a dashed line:

- in cards, a dashed card titled **Left here** and the time, like **Left here · 14:32**,
- in the plot, a dashed ring,
- in the mini multiverse, a dashed hollow dot.

## Use a snapshot

Select it. The panel says **Where you jumped from** and offers:

- **Play from here** loads that board again.
- **Keep as node** turns it into a real node where it hangs, named like **Turn 9 - Player 1 (kept 14:32)**. Then you can rename it and write a note.
- The bin discards it. The toast offers **Undo**.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Good to know

- Only the last five snapshots are kept. A sixth pushes out the oldest, so keep the ones that matter as nodes.
- A snapshot isn't a node until you keep it: it can't be renamed and has no note.

articles.title: Cards and plot
articles.summary: Switch between full node cards and the plot, where every saved turn is a dot.
articles.body:
The Multiverse draws the tree two ways: as cards, full nodes you can read, or as the plot, where every saved turn is a dot so you can see a whole game at once.

## Switch between cards and plot

:::desktop
Click **Plot** in the Multiverse header; it stays dark while the plot is on. Click it again for the cards.
:::

:::phone
Tap **Plot** (the grid of dots) in the Multiverse header, left of ✕. A phone opens on the plot until you pick a view.
:::

The Dojo remembers your choice.

[Show me](show:plot-toggle)

## Read the plot

- Each saved turn is a dot in its deck's two inks: **Player 1 solid, Player 2 striped**. Its turn number sits under it.
- A ruler along the top gives the turn and whose step each column is (**P1**, **P2**).
- Lines run from each turn to the next. The path to the node you're on is highlighted; "Left here" snapshots hang on dashed lines.
- **You are here:** a ring around the dot your board came from.
- **Cursor:** a crosshair on the selected dot, with a tag like **T12 · P1 · 7–6** (turn, player, lore).
- **20 lore · branch closed:** a won branch ends in a square dot, a bar, the winner's lore and who won.
- **Left here:** a dashed ring.

A key names all of these: along the foot of the canvas on desktop, along its top on a phone.

[Show me](show:tree-legend)

## Good to know

- Click or tap a dot to select it, as with a card. The panel shows it.
- On desktop the plot opens fitted to the whole game. A phone opens it up close, on the cursor; the zoom out thumb key shows the whole game (see [Moving around](help:multiverse-navigate)).
- The cards show more of each turn; the plot shows the shape of the game.

articles.title: Moving around: keys, thumb keys, zoom
articles.summary: Pan, zoom, and step through turns and lines with the arrow keys or the thumb keys.
articles.body:
Move around the Multiverse canvas, and step the selection through turns and lines to find the one you want. Nothing loads until you press **Play from here**.

## Pan and zoom

:::desktop
Drag the canvas to pan. Scroll to zoom in or out at the pointer. **Reset zoom** (the button left of ✕) fits the whole plot; in cards it goes back to full size at the start of the tree.

[Show me](show:tree-zoom-reset)
:::

:::phone
Drag with one finger to pan, {gesture:pinch} to zoom.
:::

## Arrow keys

:::desktop
The arrow keys move the selection, and the canvas follows it:

- {key:←} the turn before.
- {key:→} the turn after (the oldest one, if the line branches there).
- {key:↑} {key:↓} the next branch up or down from the same node.
- {key:Enter} plays from the selected node.
:::

## Thumb keys

:::phone
Six keys sit at the canvas's foot. They move the cursor, and the panel under the canvas shows the turn it's on.

- **◀** the turn before. **▶** the turn after: back the way you came, else along the line you're on.
- **▲** **▼** the nearest turn on another line above or below, near the same point in the game.
- **◎** back to the node you're on.
- **Zoom out** (the magnifier) fits the whole game. Press it again, or step, to come back in close. It's there in the plot only.

Hold an arrow to keep stepping. A key that can't go anywhere is hollow.

[Show me](show:tree-keys)
:::

## Good to know

- Opening the Multiverse selects the node you're on (or the newest) and centres on it.
- On desktop, the [mini multiverse](help:mini-multiverse) in the side rail steps through the tree and loads each turn straight away.

articles.title: The mini multiverse
articles.summary: The small map beside the board: click a dot to jump, step through a line, find branch points.
articles.body:
The mini multiverse is a small map of the whole tree in the side rail, under the players. Jump to any turn with one click, or step through a line, without opening the full Multiverse.

%%%TODO: ADD SCREENSHOT%%%%


## Read the map

- Each dot is a saved turn; each row is a line. A branch takes the nearest free row.
- The line you're on is highlighted, with filled dots. Turns ahead of you on it (a line you stepped back along) are dashed rings.
- The node you're on has a ring, dashed once the board has changed since it.
- "Left here" snapshots are dashed hollow dots. A won branch ends in a square dot and a bar.
- The head reads like **T14 · P2 · 8–8** (turn, player, lore) for the node you're on, or the dot under the pointer, whose name shows at the foot.
- **Edited · kept if you jump** at the foot means your board has changed since its node.

[Show me](show:mini-multiverse)

## Jump to a turn

Click a dot: the board becomes that turn straight away, with no **Play from here**. Drag or scroll the map to pan. The button in the head opens the full Multiverse.

## Step through a line

The keys under the map load the turn they step to:

- **⏮** back to the last branch point behind you, or the start.
- **◀** the turn before. **▶** the next turn on the line.
- **⏭** on to the next branch point ahead, or the end of the line.
- **↑** **↓** the nearest turn on the line above or below.

Click the map first and {key:←} {key:→} {key:↑} {key:↓}, {key:Home} and {key:End} do the same.

[Show me](show:mini-multiverse-keys)

## Good to know

- Stepping back keeps the rest of the line ahead of you, so **▶** retraces it.
- On a board you've changed since its node, **◀** reloads that node and **▶** goes on to the next turn.
- A board you leave unsaved is kept as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here).
- Phones don't show the map. Use the [thumb keys](help:multiverse-navigate) in the Multiverse instead.

articles.title: Study a Duels.ink game
articles.summary: Paste or drop a Duels.ink log or replay and the Dojo rebuilds the game turn by turn as a Multiverse.
articles.body:
Bring a game you played on Duels.ink into the Dojo to look at it turn by turn and try other lines from any point.

## Bring in a game

1. Open the home screen.
2. Paste the game's text log into the field, or press **Choose a file** for a replay file. You can also drop a file anywhere on the page.
3. The readout says what it found: a **Duels.ink log** with its number of turns, or a **Duels.ink replay** with the players' names.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:readout)

No game to hand? Press **A Duels.ink log** under the field to load an example.

## What you get

- A new session named after the players or their inks, with *(Duels.ink)* at the end.
- One Multiverse node per turn, with the turn's moves in its note and its card sections (played, inked, drawn and so on).
- The board at the end of the game.

Open **Multiverse**, pick a turn and press **Play from here** to load it, then play it differently. See [The Multiverse](help:multiverse).

## Good to know

- A replay file rebuilds the game most exactly. A text log is fine too. Compare them in [Import a text log](help:import-log) and [Import a replay file](help:import-replay).
- Some cards stay unknown: see [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
- The Dojo can't fetch games from Duels.ink by itself. Copy or download the game there first.

articles.title: Import a text log
articles.summary: Copy the match log from Duels.ink and paste it into the home screen or the Multiverse's Log tool.
articles.body:
A Duels.ink text log lists every move of a game. Paste it into the Dojo and every turn becomes a node in the Multiverse.

## From the home screen

1. Copy the whole log from Duels.ink.
2. Paste it into the field on the home screen. You can paste anywhere on the page; it lands in the field.
3. Check the readout: **Duels.ink log** and *A N-turn game*.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:intake)

A log saved as a .txt or .md file works too: press **Choose a file**.

## From the Multiverse

Open **Multiverse** and press **Log** in its header. Paste the log into **Import Duels.ink Log** (or choose a file). When the message under it says the log is valid, press **Import**. The game opens as a new session; the one you were in stays in your Library.

[Show me](show:tree-log)

## Which logs work

Both of Duels.ink's formats: the newer one that says *You* and *Opponent*, and the older one with *Player 1* and *Player 2*. The log needs its `--- Turn 1 ---` lines; without the starting hand lines it still imports, with a warning that fewer cards can be placed.

## Good to know

- In the Dojo, the log's owner (*You*) is Player 1.
- The newer log hides the opponent's hand and draws. See [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
- Cards the log never names come in as unknown cards: see [Unknown cards](help:unknown-cards).

articles.title: Import a replay file
articles.summary: Drop the replay file Duels.ink gives you (.json, .replay or .replay.gz) for the most exact rebuild.
articles.body:
A Duels.ink replay file records the game exactly. It's the best way to bring a game in: your own deck comes through card for card, in order.

## Import it

1. Download the replay from Duels.ink. It usually ends in **.replay.gz**; there's no need to unzip it.
2. On the home screen, press **Choose a file** and pick it, or drop the file anywhere on the page.
3. The readout shows **Duels.ink replay**, the two players and the number of turns.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:intake-file)

You can also open **Multiverse**, press **Log**, choose the file and press **Import**.

## Play your deck from it

The readout's **Play my deck from it** seats the deck you played as **You**, ready for a new match. To keep that deck, use **From a replay** in the Library's **Decks** tab: see [Your decks](help:decks).

## Good to know

- The players keep their Duels.ink names, and each keeps their Duels.ink seat: if you were the second player, you're Player 2.
- Your deck is exact, in its real order. The opponent's hidden cards stay unknown until they show them: see [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
- Only replay files carry a decklist. A text log can't give you **Play my deck from it**.

articles.title: What an import knows and doesn't
articles.summary: Your own deck is exact from a replay; the opponent's hidden cards stay unknown until they reveal them.
articles.body:
An import can only show what the game showed. Anything nobody saw comes in as an [unknown card](help:unknown-cards).

## From a replay file

- **Your deck** is exact: every card, in the order you'd have drawn it.
- **The opponent's hand and deck** are hidden. Cards they play, ink or show later are put back into their hand and deck in the earlier turns: soonest first in the hand, the rest in the deck. Cards they never show stay unknown.

## From a text log

- **Your deck**: the cards you go on to draw are on top, in order. The rest of the deck was never named, so it's unknown.
- **The opponent**, in the newer *You / Opponent* log: their opening hand and draws are hidden. As with a replay, cards they reveal later are filled in; the rest stay unknown.
- In the older *Player 1 / Player 2* log both hands are shown, so both sides work like your own.
- A card put into the inkwell or under a character face down isn't named either.

## Good to know

- Where the opponent's hidden cards sit (hand or deck) is the Dojo's best guess, not a fact.
- A text log can miss a step a replay has, such as an ability that exerts a character without naming it.
- Fix anything you know better: [swap cards](help:swap-cards) in a hand, or replace them in the deck.

articles.title: Sessions save themselves
articles.summary: Every match is a session, kept on this device as you play, and listed under Pick up again.
articles.body:
A session is one match with its whole Multiverse. The Dojo keeps every session on this device as you play, so you never lose a match by closing the tab.

## What makes a session

A new session starts when you:

- press **Start match** on the home screen,
- open a saved session file,
- study a Duels.ink log or replay,
- open a demo (it opens as your own copy).

It gets a name from the decks, like *Amber/Steel vs Ruby/Sapphire*. You can rename it: see [Save, save as copy, rename](help:save-and-rename).

## Saving happens by itself

Every change you make is saved to this device about a second later, and again when you switch tabs or close the page. You don't have to press **Save**. Leaving to the home screen keeps the match too.

## Pick up again

The home screen's **Pick up again** box lists your last session first (**Resume**), then your most recent ones, then the demos (**Explore**). The match on the board says **Back to it**. **All sessions** opens the [Library](help:library) with every session you have.

[Show me](show:recent)

## Good to know

- Sessions live in this browser on this device. Clearing the site's data or closing a private window deletes them, and another browser or device doesn't have them. Export a file to keep a backup, or [sign in](help:account) to keep them in an account. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).
- **Auto-save every turn** (in the side rail, or the ☰ menu on a phone) is different: it saves a node in the [Multiverse](help:auto-save) at each turn.
- If the Dojo can't save to this device, it tells you once: "Couldn't save to this device. Export the session to keep it."

articles.title: Save, save as copy, rename
articles.summary: Name the session, save it now, or save a copy to try something without touching the original.
articles.body:
Give the match on the board a name, save it on the spot, or split off a copy to try a different idea.

## Rename the session

:::desktop
Click the session title at the top left of the top bar, type a new name and press {key:Enter}. {key:Esc} puts the old name back.

[Show me](show:session-title)
:::

:::phone
The top bar has no title on a phone. Tap **⋯** › **Leave to the dojo** (the match stays saved), open **Library**, then the session's **⋯** › **Rename**.
:::

You can rename any session the same way from the [Library](help:library): **⋯** › **Rename**.

## Save now

The Dojo already saves as you play (see [Sessions save themselves](help:sessions)). **Save** writes it straight away and tells you so. If you're signed in, it also saves the session to your account: see [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::desktop
Press the floppy-disk button next to the title.

[Show me](show:save)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Save**.
:::

## Save as copy

Use it before trying a risky line: the copy carries on, and the original stays as it was.

:::desktop
Press the copy button next to **Save**.
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯**, then **Save as copy**.
:::

Name the copy and press **Save copy**. The copy becomes the session on the board. The original keeps everything up to that moment.

## Good to know

- A new copy is only on this device. Signed in, press **Save** to put it in your account too.
- To copy a session without opening it, use **⋯** › **Duplicate** in the Library.
- Viewing someone's shared link, **Save** saves your own copy of it. See [Open a link someone sent you](help:open-a-shared-link).

articles.title: The Library: sessions, decks, links
articles.summary: Everything you keep, on shelves by where it lives: this device, your account, built in, public links.
articles.body:
The Library holds every session and deck you keep, sorted onto shelves by where each one lives.

## Open the Library

On the home screen, press **Library** at the top, or **All sessions** in **Pick up again**. The figures on the button count your sessions on this device and, signed in, in your account. {key:Esc} or **×** closes it.

[Show me](show:library-button)

From a match, leave to the home screen first (see [The screen at a glance](help:screen-at-a-glance)).

## Three tabs

- **Sessions**: every match you've kept. **Open** loads one (**Back to it** for the match on the board). Its **⋯** menu has **Rename**, **Share a link**, **Duplicate**, **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)** and **Delete…**. **Import file** adds a session file: see [Export and import session files](help:files).
- **Decks**: your decks and the **Built in** ones. **You** and **Opponent** seat a deck for the next match. **New deck**, **Import .txt** and **From a replay** add one. See [Your decks](help:decks).
- **Links**: the share links you made, under **Public links**. See [Share a deck or a session](help:share-links).

## The shelves

Signed out, your sessions and decks sit on **On this device**, with an empty **Your account** shelf that offers **Sign in**. Signed in, they sort into **In your account + this device**, **Only on this device** and **Only in your account**. Each shelf says in one line what that means.

A row only adds a note when it's out of step, like **Changed here since your last Save**. See [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::phone
Each row's buttons sit at the foot of its card.
:::

## Good to know

- **Delete…** on a session or deck can't be undone. Export a session first if you might want it back.
- **On this device** means this browser only: clearing its site data deletes them. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).

articles.title: Export and import session files
articles.summary: Save a session as a file to back it up or send it, and open a session file.
articles.body:
A session file holds a whole match: the board, every Multiverse node, the notes and the log. Export one to keep a backup outside this browser, or to send it to someone by hand.

## Export a session

- **The match on the board:** open the **Multiverse** and press **Export** at the top.
- **Any session:** in the Library, open the session's **⋯** and choose **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)**.

:::phone
In the Multiverse the file tools show only their icons: **Export** is the file with an arrow pointing out.
:::

[Show me](show:tree-export)

The file is named after the session, like `T8 study.dojo.json.gz` (characters a file name can't hold, such as `/`, are left out). It's compressed, so even a big Multiverse stays small. A browser that can't compress saves a plain `.dojo.json` instead.

## Open a session file

Any of these works:

- On the home screen, press **Choose a file**, or drop the file anywhere on the page. The Dojo reads it and shows **Saved session**. Press **Open it**.
- In the Library's **Sessions** tab, press **Import file**.
- In the Multiverse, press **Import**.

[Show me](show:intake-file)

The Dojo reads `.dojo.json.gz`, `.dojo.json` and older `.json` session files.

## Good to know

- Opening a file always adds a new session to your library and puts it on the board. Opening the same file twice gives you two sessions.
- Your files never go anywhere unless you send them. To send a match without a file, make a [share link](help:share-links).
- A file made by a newer Dojo asks you to reload the page to update first.

articles.title: Share a deck or a session
articles.summary: Make a short link to a deck or a whole multiverse; anyone can open it, no account needed.

headings.text: Share the match on the board

articles.body:
A share link sends a deck, or a whole match with its Multiverse, to anyone. They open it in their browser; neither of you needs an account.

## Share the match on the board

:::desktop
Press the share button next to **Save** in the top bar.

[Show me](show:share)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Share link**.
:::

## Share from the Library

- **A session:** in **Sessions**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**.
- **A deck:** in **Decks**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**. Built-in decks can be shared too.

## Copy the link

When it's ready, the **Link ready** box shows a short link like `practicedojo.win/app/?s=k3J9xQ2mPa`. Press **Copy link**, then paste it wherever you like.

## See and delete your links

The Library's **Links** tab lists your links under **Public links**. Press **Copy link** to copy one again. Its **⋯** has **Open in a new tab** and **Delete link**. A deleted link stops working for everyone: it opens as "This share is no longer available".

[Show me](show:lib-links)

## Good to know

- A link is a snapshot. Later changes aren't in it, so share again to send a newer version.
- Anyone who has the link can open it. A session link carries everything in the session, including your notes.
- Making a link needs a connection. The first time, the Dojo quietly gives this browser its own sharing identity; there's no sign-in screen.
- Signed out, the **Links** tab lists the links made from this browser, and clearing its site data loses that list (the links keep working). Signed in, links belong to your account, and links this browser made before you signed in come with you (unless that Discord or Google account was already a Dojo account).
- There are limits: 20 links a day, 100 in all, and sessions up to 10 MB compressed. See [Share link limits](help:share-limits).

articles.title: Open a link someone sent you
articles.summary: A shared session opens on the board unsaved until you save a copy; a shared deck lands on the home screen.
articles.body:
Open the link in your browser. You don't need an account, and nothing is saved until you choose to keep it.

## A shared session

The match opens on the board with a bar at the top: **Shared** · its title · **not saved yet** · **Save a copy**.

[Show me](show:shared-banner)

Look around, play on, open the Multiverse. While the bar shows, nothing goes into your library. To keep it, press **Save a copy** (**Save** in the top bar does the same). It becomes your own session on this device, under the same title, and saves itself from then on like any other.

If you open something else instead, or reload the page, your changes to the shared match are gone. A reload opens the link again from the start.

## A shared deck

The Dojo opens the home screen with the deck in the paste field, marked **Shared deck** with its name. Press **Play it as you** or **Play against it** to seat it, or **Save to My decks** to keep it.

[Show me](show:intake)

## If it doesn't open

- **Link not recognised:** part of the link is missing. Ask for it again, or check you copied all of it.
- **This share is no longer available:** the person who shared it deleted it.
- **Couldn't open the link:** the Dojo couldn't reach the sharing service. Check your connection and try again.

## Good to know

- Your copy is yours. Changing it never changes the link or the sharer's session.
- A shared link is a snapshot of the moment it was made. If they keep playing, ask for a new link.
